tracks.title: Esok Datang, Bang Lah
tracks.subject: a kampung family whose rotten serambi floorboard has been propped on a paint tin for six weeks because the village handyman Bang Lah answers every call with 'esok'

tracks.title: Hutang Lima Puluh
tracks.subject: a guy whose best friend has owed him fifty ringgit for two years and keeps paying it off one teh tarik at a time at the mamak, adding up the tab out loud

tracks.title: Nasi Goreng Pukul Sebelas
tracks.subject: a man who wakes his wife at eleven at night because he has made nasi goreng kampung with too much cili padi for no reason at all, and they eat it on the kitchen floor

tracks.title: Zink Atas Kepala
tracks.subject: two old friends replacing the rusted zinc roof sheets of a kampung house on one Saturday, one on the roof counting screws, the other on the ladder passing sheets up

tracks.title: Bubur Untuk Seorang
tracks.genre: Malay yacht rock (West Coast AOR soft rock)
tracks.subject: a woman living alone who suddenly boils a full periuk of bubur kacang hijau on a Tuesday afternoon for no occasion and spends the week eating it at every meal

tracks.title: Ayah Paling Sado
tracks.subject: a 54-year-old school gardener from Alor Setar in the over-50 masters category of the Kedah state bodybuilding championship, spray-tanned the colour of teh tarik by his wife backstage, his children holding up a banner reading 'Ayah Paling Sado', placing third out of three entrants and lifting the trophy anyway

tracks.title: Seberang Papan
tracks.subject: a wife and husband married thirty-eight years, partners in the veterans' mixed-doubles carrom final at an Ipoh community hall, sitting across the board from each other as doubles partners must, where she reads his raised eyebrow before every flick, the opposing pair whispers that they must have secret signals, and on the last board she pots the red queen and covers it on his nod

tracks.title: Main Je, Uncle
tracks.subject: a woman piano tuner in Kuala Lumpur called to an old hotel on Jalan Raja Laut whose lobby grand has not been tuned in seven years, who sits on the lobby sofa the evening before and hears the one thing wrong with it: Uncle Stanley, the lobby pianist, has been playing every song around a dead F sharp for seven years; she fits a new string, raises the pitch in two passes, and the next evening waits for his hand to land on the note

tracks.title: Kira Kepala, Faiz!
tracks.genre: Malay musical-theatre showtune (teater muzikal ensemble number)
tracks.subject: a young Malaysian tour guide counting heads on the Great Wall at Badaling on a packed October holiday-week day, with twenty-eight mak ciks from Tanjung Karang in matching purple tudung, one pulled into a Henan family's holiday photos, one reaching the North Eighth Tower alone ahead of everyone, one demanding her climbing certificate say 'srikandi' instead of 'hero', and the count always one short

tracks.title: Bawah Sepuluh
tracks.subject: a seventeen-year-old at a WCA Rubik's cube competition in a Subang Jaya school hall chasing his first sub-ten-second average of five, one solve lost when the cube pops a piece under a chair, the boy beside him explaining that the best and worst times get dropped

tracks.title: Tuala Merah
tracks.mood: tender, proud and a little lovesick
tracks.subject: a tower-crane operator on a Bukit Jalil building site who watches his flat through cheap binoculars from the cab forty storeys up, where his wife hangs a red towel on the balcony rail at noon every day

tracks.title: Pangkah!
tracks.subject: a 19-year-old at a gasing pangkah (striking-top) contest at the Gelanggang Seni in Kota Bharu, Kelantan, who keeps knocking his uncles' tops out of the ring, talks trash between throws, and leaves his own top spinning longer than the emcee's patience lasts

tracks.title: Lagi! Lagi!
tracks.subject: a young woman who runs the pirate-ship swing at a travelling funfair on a town padang, pushing it higher every time the kids scream 'lagi', and on the last night gives a free ride to the boy in blue slippers who watched every night without a ticket

tracks.title: Tak Boleh Bungkus
tracks.subject: a coconut seller on the Teluk Cempedak beach road in Kuantan who refuses to let anyone take a coconut away, making a customer in a hurry sit on his plastic stool and drink it there

tracks.title: Satu Biji Lagi
tracks.subject: a grandmother in Kuala Kangsar who has never lost a game of congkak, and the twenty-eight-year-old grandson who practises on a phone app on the LRT for three months to beat her on a Sunday visit

tracks.title: Tekong Gemuk Kampung
tracks.mood: rowdy, cheeky, a whole kampung laughing
tracks.subject: the round, cheerful tekong of a kampung sepak takraw team who somehow serves them through to the district final while the whole village shouts from the drain edge

tracks.title: Milo Mesin Tingkat Tiga
tracks.subject: two night-shift nurses who meet at the third-floor vending machine every night at four for one shared can of Milo

tracks.title: Periuk Mak Jah
tracks.genre: 1950s Malay film-studio orchestral song (P. Ramlee lineage)
tracks.mood: sly, comic, polite on top and fed up underneath
tracks.subject: a man rehearsing, very politely, how to ask the neighbour to return the rice pot she borrowed three Hari Raya ago

tracks.title: Si Kelabu Lambat Lagi
tracks.genre: poetic piano chamber pop (Sal Priadi lane)
tracks.mood: wry, warm, a lump in the throat held back by a joke
tracks.subject: a retired postman who keeps racing pigeons on his flat's rooftop and waits every Sunday for the slowest bird, a grey one, long after the others are home

tracks.title: Feri Akhir Ke Lumut
tracks.mood: patient, longing, rain on still water
tracks.subject: a woman waiting at the Lumut jetty in the rain for the last ferry from Pangkor carrying her husband home from his week at the fish-drying yard
